overview: This Senate resolution names August 2 through August 8, 2026, as "National Farmers Market Week." It recognizes farmers markets, where farmers sell food directly to shoppers, for their role in local economies, in connecting city and rural communities, and in helping low-income families who use federal nutrition benefits get fresh food. It cites Agriculture Department figures showing the number of farmers markets grew sharply between 1994 and 2019. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say farmers markets help small farmers earn a living and give communities better access to fresh, local food, and deserve national recognition.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
